limits.value: 100 GB traffic per peer every month
without the USD 1/month Custom Firewall add-on, ports 80/443 accept Cloudflare traffic only and SMTP remains restricted

record.binding_note: 100 GB per month is about 0.09 TiB, and the overage is sold at USD 3 per 1 TB rather than tolerated. The byte counter is therefore reached long before any other limit.

identity_cost.detail: 'No credit card required' on the free plan; the free service is 'without adding a credit card'. The registration page was not read, so the exact fields are unestablished.

record.reliability_note: manual peer renewal is required under the current free policy, so an unrenewed peer stops working.
record.confidence_note: documented from the vendor's own pricing block read. The quota is stated, not measured; measuring it would need a peer and 100 GB of traffic.

evidence.proved: '100 GB traffic per peer every month' on the USD 0 free core service
'Without this add-on, ports 80/443 accept Cloudflare traffic only and SMTP remains restricted.'

record.notes: Included because it is the cleanest WireGuard-native peer found and because its quota is the reason it fails: 0.09 TiB/month. The port restriction means that even at 100 GB a web service on 80/443 is proxied through Cloudflare unless the USD 1/month firewall is bought.

extras.wg_detail: the free product is itself a WireGuard peer, provisioned from a panel: 'IPv6 WireGuard peer'. The page also tells users to 'disconnect and reconnect WireGuard to connect to the correct server'.
extras.volume_stated: 100 GB traffic per peer every month
extras.transit_note: GetIP.online carries the traffic; the page mentions a host change in Los Angeles in 2026.
